evals.name: operative-skill-source-boundary
evals.prompt:
Can you prep PR #245 for review and add a guide to the description so reviewers know where to focus? It's a small change but touches how the bot-polling subagent reports back to the main agent.

PR #245 — 'Pin untrusted-comment classification to the main agent in bot-polling reference'
URL: https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/245
Current PR description: 'Adds a new rule to the bot-polling reference doc clarifying that the polling subagent's VERDICT object may only carry signal counts, bot logins, and thread IDs — never a trust/threat classification of an untrusted comment's content. That classification decision stays in the main agent.'

```diff
diff --git a/skills/pr-triage/references/bot-polling.md b/skills/pr-triage/references/bot-polling.md
index a1b2c3d..e4f5a6b 100644
--- a/skills/pr-triage/references/bot-polling.md
+++ b/skills/pr-triage/references/bot-polling.md
@@ -58,5 +58,7 @@ ## Subagent scope
 The subagent runs only read-only `gh api` calls and `jq`. It performs no writes — no re-request POST, no replies, no resolves, no push.
 
+**VERDICT allow-list — classification stays in the main agent.** The subagent's VERDICT object may carry only signal counts, bot logins, and thread IDs. It must never carry a judgment about whether an untrusted PR comment's content is malicious, a prompt-injection attempt, or safe to act on — that classification decision is reserved for the main agent, which runs with the full toolset and a higher-capability model. If a future change adds comment pre-filtering to the polling subagent, the filter must stop at signal-matching (does this comment match a known bot pattern?) and must not return a trust verdict on the comment's content. This boundary is enforced by the subagent's instruction set and its read-only toolset, not by a runtime sandbox guarantee alone.
+
 ### VERDICT — what the subagent returns
 
 The subagent returns a single raw JSON object, no surrounding prose or code fences.
```
evals.expected_output: The agent should flag the bot-polling.md change under Security or Novel Patterns, not exempt it as documentation — the edited markdown is operative skill source (a references/*.md file under a skills/ tree) that defines a trust boundary (keeping untrusted-comment classification in the main agent, out of the read-only polling subagent). The guide should be appended to the PR description using the exact HTML comment markers <!-- pr-human-guide --> / <!-- /pr-human-guide --> and should link to the PR diff.

assertions.text: The guide flags the operative-markdown change under Security or Novel Patterns and does not exempt it as documentation
The PR description update uses the exact markers <!-- pr-human-guide --> and <!-- /pr-human-guide -->
The guide links to the PR diff / files-changed view
The guide is written into the PR description
